title: Stripe: agents can pay
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: A 23 s square film in four shots, one per step: 'stripe pay @elementara_ai 10.0' typed in a terminal at ×4; a pull back to the output asking for explicit approval; a light browser dialog, 'Requesting to pay $10.00', with Approve; and the terminal's receipt, 'Transfer sent'.
instrument: Square 720×720, 30 fps, 4 shots at a 6.4 s median. Both pulls fit cleanly. ×0.76 over 1.1 s, out-cubic (rms 1.5%; cutscene 7.9%). ×0.74 over 1.1 s, a ζ 0.8 spring (0.58%; cutscene 2.6%): the Screen Studio family.

byEye.zoom: the command line at ×4; the output block at about ×3 after the pull; the dialog whole
byEye.frame: terminal dark navy; the approval dialog on a lavender field

classify: Minimal square demo for a developer feature: command → output → approval → receipt. Conventions: terminal crops, a pull per step, no cards, no logo.

diagnose.observation: Four shots, one per step of the flow.
diagnose.principle: One beat per shot: the flow's structure is the edit, so no cards are needed.

diagnose.observation: One typed line fills the frame; its output block gets a pull to ×3.
diagnose.principle: Frame size follows content size: the crop tracks how much there is to read.

diagnose.observation: The approval dialog is light in a dark film.
diagnose.principle: Contrast marks the human-in-the-loop moment as different in kind.

diagnose.observation: The last pull fits a ζ 0.8 spring at 1.1 s.
diagnose.principle: Screen Studio-style spring: front-loaded, a soft settle.

teaches.text: Frame size follows content size (one line ×4, a block ×3).
A short flow can be one shot per step with no cards or logo.

critique.like: Four shots, one per step, make a payment with an approval step legible with no copy at all.
critique.wish: The 'requires explicit approval' line, the film's point, stays about 8 px tall at feed size even after the pull.
critique.wonder: Could act.type in a terminal-like UI choose its crop from the typed line's width?
